title: Queen of Pentacles Tarot Meaning: Upright & Reversed
description: Queen of Pentacles upright: nurturing, practicality, comfort; reversed: self-neglect. Love, work, money, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Ask your question.
h1: Queen of Pentacles Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Queen of Pentacles, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a crowned queen on a carved stone throne looks down at a large pentacle in her lap under an arch of roses; a rabbit in the corner.
capsule: The Queen of Pentacles means nurturing, practicality and comfort: warm care that keeps a home and a life running. Reversed, that care can turn into self-neglect, money worries or smothering. It is one of the kindest cards in the deck, as long as you count yourself among those you look after. The answer is yes: her garden is in bloom.

blocks.heading: What is on the Queen of Pentacles card?
paragraphs: A crowned queen sits on a carved stone throne in a garden, holding a large pentacle in her lap with both hands and looking down at it. Waite describes her face as that of a dark woman "whose qualities might be summed up in the idea of greatness of soul" (p. 256). Waite adds that "she contemplates her symbol and may see worlds therein" (p. 256).

On the 1909 card an arch of roses and leaves runs across the top, and flowers grow beside the throne. She wears a red gown with a green veil over her shoulders, and blue mountains and water show in the distance. A small rabbit appears in the grass in the lower right corner. The largest symbol is the pentacle in her lap, which her whole figure bends toward.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Queen of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Waite's list (p. 256) is wealth and ease: plenty, generosity, splendor, security and freedom. Waite's reversed list (p. 256) is blunt, with evil and fear next to suspicion and mistrust; on Arcana Diary that side of the card reads as worry and insecurity around money and home.
Besides greatness of soul, Waite gives her "the serious cast of intelligence" (p. 256).

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Pentacles mean upright?
paragraphs: Nurturing is this Queen's first meaning, and it is the practical kind: a meal ready, a bill paid, a room that feels good to come home to. She stands for comfort shared with others and for security built out of ordinary, well-run days. Practicality is part of her warmth, not its opposite.

The card can come up when you are the one who looks after others, at home or at work, or when life calls for down-to-earth care: sorting the household, making a space pleasant, helping someone in a concrete way. It also asks whether any of that care reaches you. Which everyday comfort have you been giving everyone except yourself?

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Pentacles mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the Queen's care loses its balance. It can flow outward until nothing is left for you, which is self-neglect, or tighten into smothering: looking after people so closely that they have no room. Money worries about the home may take up too much space, or work and home may fall into imbalance, one eating the other.

Suspicion and mistrust from Waite's reversed list (p. 256) fit the insecure side of this; the rest is a modern reading, not Waite's. One small, practical thing done for your own comfort is a good place to restart.

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Pentacles mean in love?
paragraphs: Between partners, the Queen of Pentacles is love shown through care you can touch: a meal made, a home made cozy, steady support on ordinary days. It speaks of a secure, generous bond where both people feel looked after.

Without a partner, the card turns to the warmth you already give friends and family, and to making your own life comfortable first. Reversed, care can become one-sided: giving everything, or feeling taken for granted. Accepting help is part of this card too.

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Pentacles mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Nurturing reaches the bank account as well: financial security, a household budget that covers the essentials and leaves something for comfort, resources handled wisely and shared generously. Reversed, it can mean money worries around the home, spending too much on others, or a budget so tight it leaves no room for small pleasures.
In a job, the card describes the person who keeps things running and looks after the people too: organized, practical, kind. It suits work that makes daily life better for someone.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Queen of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Tidy one corner of your home and make it a little more comfortable: better light, something soft, a plant. Then actually use it. For this Queen, comfort is not a reward for finishing everything; it is part of what keeps you able to care for others.

blocks.heading: Is the Queen of Pentacles a yes or no card?
The Queen of Pentacles as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Seated in her garden with a coin in her lap, the Queen of Pentacles is warm, practical and generous: someone who makes others feel at home, manages resources well and helps in concrete ways; it can be a parent figure, a friend, a colleague or you. Feeling-wise, the card stands for devoted, caring affection: feeling safe with someone, wanting to look after them and to build a comfortable life together. Reversed, the same care can feel smothering or one-sided, or worry and insecurity crowd out the warmth.

blocks.heading: The Queen of Pentacles with other cards

pairs.text: A secure home and family ties: care that builds something lasting.
A hard stretch met with practical care. Help, given or received, makes the difference.
Two steady providers: a shared life on solid footing, generous on both sides.
Warm memories and home comforts; kindness from family or old friends.

blocks.heading: Queen of Pentacles, Nine of Pentacles or The Empress?
paragraphs: Waite describes the Nine of Pentacles as "a woman, with a bird upon her wrist" among grapevines in a manor garden (p. 264); today it means independence and enjoying what you earned yourself. The Queen's comfort is shared with others; the Nine's is personal and self-made.

In Waite's description, a field of corn ripens in front of The Empress, with "a fall of water" beyond (p. 80); today she means abundance and creativity on a wide scale. The Queen of Pentacles brings the same warmth down to one home and one budget.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Queen of Pentacles
paragraphs: Who receives my care, and am I on that list?
What would make my home feel more like a place to rest?
Where could practical help say more than words?

faq.q: Is the Queen of Pentacles a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good. It is among the most comforting cards a reading can show: security, generosity and a life looked after with care. Its harder side appears only when that care stops reaching you or tightens into control, and both ease with small, practical changes.

faq.q: Does the Queen of Pentacles mean money?
faq.a: Partly. Money appears in this card as security and wise handling of resources, not as sudden wealth. Waite himself notes that the Pentacles cards do not deal especially with questions of money (p. 254), and this Queen's meaning reaches past cash to home, comfort and care.

faq.q: What does the rabbit on the Queen of Pentacles mean?
faq.a: Waite never mentions it: his description of this Queen covers only her face and her gaze on the coin (p. 256). The rabbit is part of the drawing, a small animal in the grass at the edge of the scene, so this page does not give it a meaning of its own.

faq.q: Is the Queen of Pentacles a mother figure?
faq.a: She is often read that way today, because her meaning is nurturing and a well-kept home. Still, the card describes a way of caring, not a family role: anyone of any age can take it on, including you whenever you look after others.

waite.quote: Opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, liberty. Reversed: Evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, mistrust.
